No, it's not. UTF-16 supports the same characters as UTF-32 and UTF-8 (all three support all of Unicode). UTF-16 does that by having... variable width characters, in the form of 2-UTF16 code units for some chars.

UTF-8 tries to optimize space (but is ASCII skewed) with more variance (but once you can't infer length from bytes, what's the difference?) UTF-32 is a space hog at the benefit of predictable length encoding (a full Int32 to represent the null char, or a carriage return)
